tools.blocked_reason:
BLOCKED, and the reason is a PRECONDITION THAT IS ITSELF A CARD.

Surfaced 5/5 and called 4/5 (2 runs lost to transport errors, which are never model results). Every call was refused, and the refusal is a GOOD one — it names the problem, the supplier and the exact op:
    "this project has no adopted ontology to edit — call kg_list_templates to pick one, then kg_adopt_template (or kg_ontology_propose with op='adopt_template') with its source_schema_id"

MY SCENARIO WAS WRONG, NOT THE TOOL. A fresh project has edge_types=[] and no adopted ontology, so there was nothing to edit. Verified by direct probe: the canonical call (op=schema_edit, verb=add, level=edge_type, code=mentored_by) gets exactly that refusal.

🔴 AND THE FIX IS NOT AVAILABLE TO THIS LOOP. Adopting an ontology is `kg_adopt_template` (Tier W) or this tool's own op='adopt_template' (Tier W) — both confirm-gated — and there is no REST or non-gated path. So this tool's happy path sits behind ANOTHER tool's card, and the standing rule is that no card is ever approved. That is a real shippability observation, not a harness limitation: a two-card chain where the first card gates the second cannot be exercised by an agent in one sitting either.

I ALSO SUSPECTED A DEFECT THAT WAS NOT ONE. `verb` and `level` are closed sets, and my first reading of the advertised schema showed enum=None for both — which would have been the exact 'closed-set arg needs an enum' defect book-service gates. It is not: both enums ARE advertised, nested inside an `anyOf` alongside the null branch, because the parameters are Optional. Reading `properties[k].enum` at the top level misses them. That is the union-extraction trap this repo has already recorded, and it nearly produced a fix for a defect that does not exist.

Separately worth noting: the model did NOT follow the refusal's own instruction to adopt a template first — the same not-chaining-after-a-refusal behaviour DQ-T36 tracks.

🔴 THE RE-RUN DID NOT CLEAN UP EITHER. This dedicated arm was run because batch 32 lost 2 of 5 to transport errors, and it lost 2 of 5 again — 5/5 called both times, ~40% erroring both times. Twice is a CONDITION, not luck, so it is recorded rather than re-rolled indefinitely. Under the standing rule that a transport failure is never a model result, this tool stays UNCONCLUDED: the gate refuses `blocked` while the turn itself is unproven, and that refusal is correct.
